intent: Let the six lib/tests suites be gated automatically even when a suite must run inside the coverage jail. Before this, ci_mirror.sh and shell-tests.yml invoked every discovered run_all.sh bare; the features/lib suite refuses to run bare (its REFUSING guards are what stop a test run from rewriting the real /etc), so the push gate blocked all six pending commits and CI would have gone red on the same suite.
scope: meta/scripts/ci_mirror.sh: new run_jailed_suite helper + branch in run_shell_test_gate
.github/workflows/shell-tests.yml: same branch in the 'Run lib/tests suites' step; kcov added to the install step
Non-goal: the REFUSING guards are untouched -- they are load-bearing safety, not an obstacle
Non-goal: no change to shell_coverage_jail.sh or check_shell_coverage.sh
changes: The jail requirement is now DECLARED BY THE SUITE as a jail_args file beside run_all.sh, holding the --bind/--seed-dir/--seed-file/--timeout flags it needs. Both consumers do one find, then branch on the marker's presence, so adding a jail-requiring suite needs no edit to either runner.

Chose data-over-path-list deliberately: the 105 remaining allowlisted libs were scored on root ops and system writes, so most future suites will need the jail too. Hardcoding features/lib in two runners would drift -- the exact failure ci_mirror.sh's own comments say it exists to prevent.
Both branches fail closed: a jail_args present but empty is reported as a configuration error, never silently skipped.
The flags previously trapped in run_all.sh's header comment are now executable data rather than prose.

verification.evidence: dot_resolver_install.sh: 39/39 lines = 100.00% -- the args file reproduces the handoff's independently measured figure, confirming the extracted flags are correct and complete.

verification.command: for r in <the five unmarked runners>; do timeout 120s "$r"; done
verification.evidence: PASS on all five: scripts/lib, digital_wellbeing/lib, hosts/lib, periodic_background/lib, single_use/utils/lib. Confirms only features/lib needs the jail, so the bare branch stays correct for the others.
syntax OK; shellcheck emitted no findings. No suppressions added.

verification.command: git push origin main (pre-push: prettier + ci-mirror)
verification.evidence: ci-mirror previously failed with 'REFUSING: this suite must run under shell_coverage_jail.sh' + 'lib/tests suite failed: .../features/lib/tests/run_all.sh'. After the fix the same gate runs the marked suite through the jail and the push completes.

risks: CI now needs kcov on ubuntu-latest; it is apt-installable and added to the existing install step, but an apt outage turns the shell-tests job red for an infrastructure reason rather than a code one.

A new jail-requiring suite that forgets its jail_args file will be run bare and fail loudly via its own REFUSING guard. That is the intended direction (loud, not silent), but the failure names the guard rather than the missing marker.
jail_args is positional shell words, one per line; a flag and its value on the same line would be passed as a single argument and the jail would reject it.
rollback: git revert the commit: both runners return to invoking every runner bare, and the jail_args marker disappears.
After rollback, re-verify that pushing is blocked again by the features/lib suite -- that block is the symptom this commit removes, so its return confirms a clean revert.
